question: Why do persons arise even when the supreme Lord remains full?
premises: The supreme Lord remains full even when personhood is assumed.
In that state there is non-recognition of his own nature.
This non-recognition is described as wondrous.
inference: Personhood arises through a wondrous non-recognition of the Lord's own full nature.
plain_english: Thus, even though the supreme Lord remains full, when personhood is assumed there arises a wondrous non-recognition of his own nature; from that come persons.
